question: Evidence that a backup restoration test was completed during the audit period, including the test plan, the result, and any follow-up items raised.
A complete list of application and infrastructure changes released during the audit period, covering both GitHub pull requests and env0 deployment runs.
Documentation showing that separate staging and production environments exist for the in-scope application, GitHub, RDS, and Snowflake, including an env0 environment inventory.

The policy and procedure covering scheduled job management: how schedules are created and modified, what approvals are required before a job runs in production, and which tools confirm that jobs ran as scheduled.
A list of jobs scheduled in production during the audit period.
The most recent privileged and non-privileged access reviews covering every in-scope system, including who performed each review and how exceptions were resolved.
A current account and role listing for each in-scope system, covering user, shared, and service accounts, with the role definitions needed to assess least privilege and separation of duties.
A list of accounts holding read-only access to the in-scope databases.
A list of accounts able to change production configuration, including env0 team and project role assignments.
A list of accounts able to deploy to production, including GitHub teams with merge rights and env0 teams with release permissions.
A list of accounts with access to the test and staging environments.
For employees who changed roles during the audit period, the records showing which access was added and which was removed. Where no change was required, a short note explaining why.
Approval records for access granted to employees who changed roles during the audit period.
A list of access additions, modifications, and removals across the in-scope systems during the audit period, including audit-log entries for group and role membership changes.
The policy and procedure for disabling inactive accounts, stating the inactivity threshold and whether enforcement is automated or manual.
Evidence that production changes were authorized and tested before release, including the approval record for a recent release.
Audit log extracts from the in-scope systems covering authentication activity (successful and failed password changes) and account creation and removal events, sampled across the audit period.
A description of how operating system patches reach servers and workstations, whether the process is automated through Kandji or another MDM, and whether updates are reviewed before installation.
A list of the people notified when an unauthorized network connection is detected, and the alert configuration that routes to them.
